title: Brand Guidelines
body:
> 🎨 **Mindcast Limited · Taupō, Aotearoa New Zealand**  
MC-BRD-001 · Version 1.0 · August 2026 · Brand & Identity
## Brand Guidelines
Mindcast is a broadcast you tune into with other people in a room. Everything we make should feel like a clear signal — calm, deliberate, human, and never shouting.
**Document owner:** Founder (Ashleigh Carlson)  
**Applies to:** All staff, contractors, agencies  
**Next review:** August 2027  
**Status:** Live
## 1 · The idea behind the identity
Mindcast is not a podcast, an app, or a course. It is a weekly gathering where a signal is transmitted and received in person. The broadcast metaphor is analogue: a radio dial, a level meter, a tuning needle finding a station. Warm, patient, physical.
The visual line is **navy ink on ivory paper, with one blue signal running through it.**
> _Tune into your inner self. Awareness into action, together._
Three rules govern everything:
1. **One accent, used sparingly.** Signal Blue earns attention because it is rare.
1. **Type does the work.** Bebas Neue set large and tight is the loudest thing we do; decoration is secondary.
1. **No pressure.** No urgency banners, countdowns, manufactured scarcity or guilt. The voice invites; it does not sell through pressure.
## 2 · Colour
The source of truth is `src/index.css`. Do not introduce a hard-coded brand colour outside this system unless explicitly documented.
### Core palette
- **Ink Navy — **`**#102438**` — primary text, footers, table headers; token `--navy`.
- **Signal Blue — **`**#3585AF**` — accent, links, active states, signal bar and focus rings; token `--blue`.
- **Signal Deep — **`**#307191**` — filled buttons, pressed/hover states and small coloured text; token `--primary`.
- **Ivory — **`**#FFFAF5**` — primary page background; token `--ivory` / `--cream`.
- **Navy Mid — **`**#1C3E5A**` — secondary text, pull quotes and subheads.
- **Mist — **`**#C5E3F3**` — tints, inactive signal segments, chart fills and quiet surfaces.
### Supporting palette
- **Deep Navy — **`**#0A1120**` — admin console/facilitator dark surface only.
- **Slate — **`**#8E9299**` — muted labels on dark surfaces.
- **Silver — **`**#7B929D**` — muted labels on light surfaces, captions and metadata.
- **Line — **`**#E1E7EF**` — rules, borders and dividers.
- **Paper — **`**#FFFFFF**` — cards/documents sitting on Ivory.
### Functional status colours only
Active `#10B981` · Trialling `#0EA5E9` · Past due `#F59E0B` · Paused `#64748B` · Error `#EF4444`.
**Bronze is retired.** Any legacy `--bronze` reference aliases to Signal Blue. Do not reintroduce gold/bronze; it pushes the identity toward luxury/spiritual-guru territory.
### Usage ratio
Aim for approximately **70% Ivory / 22% Ink Navy / 6% Mist / 2% Signal Blue**. If a layout feels flat, use more whitespace and stronger hierarchy rather than more blue.
### Accessibility
- Ink Navy on Ivory ≈ 14.8:1 — AAA.
- Signal Deep on Ivory ≈ 4.9:1 — use for body-size coloured text.
- Signal Blue on Ivory ≈ 3.9:1 — large text/non-text UI only.
- White on Signal Deep ≈ 4.6:1 — AA.
- Every interactive control requires a visible `2px solid #3585AF` focus ring with `2px` offset.
## 3 · Typography
**Bebas Neue — Display.** Headings, titles, wordmark, navigation labels and statistics. Uppercase; tracking roughly `0.02em–0.14em`. Never running body text or below 11px.
**Montserrat — Body.** Reading text, forms, tables, UI and buttons. Body 15–16px, line-height about 1.72 and max line length around 74 characters.
**Cormorant Garamond — Voice.** Human moments: pull quotes, title standfirsts, affirmations and selected testimonials. Usually italic; never functional UI or legal text.
**Inter — Utility only.** Dense numeric/admin tables where needed; not member-facing brand copy.
**Type scale:** 10 · 12 · 13 · 15 · 18 · 22 · 26 · 32 · 44 · 52 px.
## 4 · The signal bar
The signature device appears on every controlled document, deck and letterhead: **18 vertical segments** like a broadcast meter. The first seven are Signal Blue, the remainder Mist. Segment heights: **30 · 44 · 58 · 72 · 86 · 100 · 86**, then a flat **34** for the tail.
Meaning: **the signal is being received, and there is room to grow.** Use 14–16px height, full content width, 3px gaps, directly beneath the wordmark. Never recolour it, invert it to gold, or animate it in printed/legal contexts.
## 5 · Wordmark
`Mind` in Ink Navy + `cast` in Signal Blue, Bebas Neue, uppercase, tracking `0.10em`; one word, no space.
- Clear space: at least the cap-height of the M on every side.
- Minimum size: 90px screen / 24mm print.
- Dark surface: Mind in Ivory; cast remains Signal Blue.
- Single-colour fallback: all Ink Navy or all Ivory.
- Never stretch, outline, glow, shadow, rotate, place over busy photography, add a tagline lock-up, or substitute the typeface.
## 6 · Voice and tone
We sound like a steady person who has done the work and is not selling you anything.
**We write:** “Come back in seven days.” · “This week's practice.” · “You can leave at any time.” · “Mindcast is not therapy. If you need clinical support, we'll help you find it.”
**We do not write:** “Don't miss out.” · “Unlock your potential today.” · “You'll lose your progress.” · “Transform your life in 52 weeks.” · artificial ‘investment’ framing.
Use New Zealand English: organise, colour, programme for a course of study, program for software. Use correct macrons: Taupō, Māori, kōrero, whānau. Dates: **Sunday 14 September 2026**. Currency: **$30 NZD**.
Forbidden across Mindcast surfaces: **“click here”, “subscribe now”, “limited time only”, “hurry”, “last chance”, countdown timers, fake scarcity, exit-intent pressure and guilt-based retention copy.** Never position the founder as a teacher, guru, healer or authority. We facilitate; we do not create dependency.
## 7 · Imagery
Photograph real rooms and real members where written consent permits: hands, chairs in a circle, the venue at dusk, a workbook on a knee, someone laughing mid-sentence. Natural light; restrained grain is welcome.
Avoid generic wellness/spiritual imagery: meditating beach stock, lotus flowers, mandalas, glowing brains, chakra diagrams, sunrise motivational imagery or religious/new-age iconography. A 4% grain overlay may be used on full-bleed imagery, never over text.
## 8 · Applying the brand to documents
Every controlled document uses: wordmark/entity line top-left · document ID/version/date top-right · signal bar · eyebrow → title → standfirst → control block → content → navy footer.
Document IDs: `MC-[DOMAIN]-[NNN]`: **BRD** Brand · **GOV** Governance · **MEM** Member-facing · **HR** People & employment · **SAF** Safeguarding · **SEC** Data & security · **FIN** Finance & operations · **TRN** Training.
## 9 · Assets and source of truth
- Design tokens: `src/index.css :root`
- Tailwind mapping: `tailwind.config.ts`
- Fonts: `@fontsource/*` — self-hosted; no runtime Google Fonts.
- PWA icons: `public/pwa-icon-512.png`, `public/favicon.png`
- Theme colour: `index.html` → `#3585af`
- Canva Brand Kit must mirror this document.
Anyone changing a brand colour changes `src/index.css` first and then updates this controlled document. A stray hard-coded hex in a component is a bug, not a design decision. The current admin-console dark-surface literals are the temporary documented exception pending a dark-token pass.

title: Company Charter
body:
> 
# Company Charter
**Mindcast Limited · Taupō, Aotearoa New Zealand**
MC-GOV-001 · Version 1.2 · August 2026 · Governance
Why Mindcast exists, what it promises, and the boundaries it will not cross to grow. Every other policy in the controlled document set is downstream of this document.
**Document owner:** Founder / Board
**Applies to:** Whole organisation
**Next review:** August 2027
**Status:** Live
---
## 1 · Who we are
Mindcast Limited is a New Zealand company incorporated on 26 March 2026, based in Taupō. It operates Mindcast — a weekly, in-person, facilitated gathering for personal development, running a 52-week curriculum across three parallel tracks: adults, teens and children.
We are a membership community, not a course business. Membership revenue covers the room, the people, the tools and the operating margin required to keep the business sustainable. The live Sunday gathering may be attended free; paid membership unlocks the interactive app experience and the continuing digital journey. Revenue exists to sustain and improve the gathering, while Mindcast Limited remains a transparent for-profit business.
---
## 2 · Purpose
**To help people move from unconscious patterns, to conscious awareness, to meaningful change — and to create communities where that change is practised together rather than consumed alone.**
**You are unaware, and you don't change.**
**You are aware, and you still don't change.**
**You are aware — and you do.**
**Mindcast is the room built for that third one.**
**UNCONSCIOUS → CONSCIOUS → CHANGED**
The problem we exist to solve is not a lack of information. It is the implementation gap between becoming aware of something and actually changing what you do. People can understand the pattern, finish the book, listen to the podcast and still live the same way on Friday. Content is abundant and follow-through is scarce. Mindcast supplies the missing half — structure, rhythm, action, witness, community, and a return date.
---
## 3 · Mission
**Mindcast turns awareness into action and insight into lived change. We curate the best of what has already been said, turn it into questions that make it personal, and give people a safe, structured weekly practice to understand themselves, take meaningful action and grow alongside a real community.**
Every week, the method is simple: **Notice it. Name it. Do it.**
- **Notice it** — see the pattern, reaction or behaviour that may have been operating unconsciously.
- **Name it** — put clear language around what is happening, what it is costing, and what needs to change.
- **Do it** — choose one meaningful action and practise something different in real life.
Awareness is necessary, but it is not the finish line. The purpose of the weekly practice is movement from **unconscious → conscious → changed**.
We deliver this through:
- **A weekly live gathering** — one theme, one facilitator, one screen, one hour.
- **A private reflection** — journalling that belongs to the member and no one else.
- **A midweek Life Group** — a small group that notices when you do not turn up.
- **A 52-week curriculum** — sequenced across four phases, running in parallel for adults, teens and children so whole families grow side by side.
- **A commitment loop** — set an intention, come back in seven days, and be gently held to it.
---
## 4 · Vision
**A world where every neighbourhood has a room you can walk into and become more yourself — together, and where the next generation grows up already holding the tools their parents had to go looking for.**
Taupō is the prototype. Once one full 52-week cycle is proven, documented and safe, the model may be licensed to facilitators in other towns, with curriculum, software, brand and safeguarding standards licensed from the centre.
---
## 5 · Brand promise and behaviour framework
**Brand promise:** Tune into yourself.
**Transformation:** Unconscious → Conscious → Changed.
**Behaviour framework:** Notice it. Name it. Do it.
The transformation describes the journey Mindcast exists to support. The behaviour framework is the weekly method that helps make that journey practical: notice what is happening, name it clearly, then do something different. The brand promise carries the feeling; the behaviour framework carries the method. Application rules are set out in the Brand Guidelines (MC-BRD-001).
---
## 6 · Values
**Community over content.** The room, relationships and repeated practice matter more than producing more information for people to consume.
**Autonomy over dependence.** A successful participant becomes more capable of noticing and choosing for themselves, not more dependent on Mindcast, its founder or facilitators.
**Draw out, do not preach.** Facilitators help people explore their own experience. Mindcast does not impose a belief system, deity, doctrine or dogma, and does not present any leader as the source of truth.
**Safe by design.** Safeguarding, privacy, professional boundaries, moderation and health and safety are part of the product — not administrative extras.
**Action over passive consumption.** Each week should help participants move from awareness toward one realistic action or intention they can practise.
**Everyone deserves a path to belong.** Free attendance and accessible bridge products sit alongside paid membership. Pricing and programme design aim to reduce unnecessary barriers to participation while keeping the organisation sustainable. Concessions may be offered permanently, never as pressure-based promotions.
**Honest about what we are.** Mindcast is not therapy, medicine, a church or a cure. We are explicit about our scope and refer people to qualified professional help when a need sits outside it. Not every week will land for every person, and we say so.
**No pressure, ever.** We do not use urgency, scarcity, guilt or manipulation to recruit or retain anybody.
---
## 7 · What we will not do
These are hard limits. They bind the founder, the board, every employee, contractor, volunteer and future licensee.
- We will not position any individual — including the founder — as a guru, healer, teacher or spiritual authority.
- We will not provide therapy, counselling, diagnosis, medical advice or crisis intervention. We refer.
- We will not discourage a member from leaving, use retention pressure after cancellation, or make departure socially costly.
- We will not ask members for donations beyond clearly published commercial fees, or use escalating payment tiers designed to exploit belonging.
- We will not ask anyone to reduce contact with family, friends, work or other communities.
- We will not display, publish or repurpose anything a member writes without explicit, specific, revocable consent.
- We will not sell, rent or trade member data, or use member reflections to train third-party AI models.
- We will not accept sponsorship or partnership that requires promoting a product to members.
---
## 8 · Business model
**Core engine — paid memberships.** Adult, teen and family memberships pay for interactive app participation, saved reflections, digital workbook and history, member tools, and the operational system surrounding the weekly gathering.
**Free community access.** The live Sunday session is open to attend free, subject to venue capacity and registration. A non-member may listen and take part in the room but does not receive ongoing app access or saved interactive participation.
**Bridge product.** A non-member may buy the day's physical worksheet for **$5 NZD**. This is a low-friction bridge, not the primary revenue engine.
**Founding offer.** Working commercial assumption: first 100 adult memberships at **$29 NZD/week**, price locked for 12 months; standard adult membership **$35 NZD/week** thereafter. Youth and family pricing is approved separately before launch.
**Products.** Printed workbooks, session handouts, and replacement or additional NFC bracelets.
**Licensing — after proof.** Curriculum, software and brand standards may be licensed to facilitators in other towns only after Taupō has completed a safe and documented full cycle and governance approves the model.
**Cost drivers.** Venue, paid facilitators and session staff, insurance, software and infrastructure, printing, vetting, training, professional review, and administration.
**Financial principle.** Core operational roles should become paid as early as practicable. Genuine volunteers may support peripheral community activity, but unpaid labour must not become the economic foundation of the for-profit operating model.
---
## 9 · Legal and structural position
Mindcast Limited holds the intellectual property, software, contracts and licensing rights. The founder is the sole director at incorporation.
An open structural decision is whether a local community arm should ever sit inside a separate charitable trust or incorporated society while Mindcast Limited licenses curriculum and software to it. This is **not** the current operating model and must not blur the fact that Mindcast Limited is a transparent for-profit business.
Any future community-arm structure must be decided with a New Zealand lawyer and accountant before grant applications or a first licensee. Until then Mindcast operates wholly as a limited company.
---
## 10 · Governance commitments
- Independent Advisory Group of at least three people, none employees or family of the founder, meeting at least twice a year.
- Named Safeguarding Lead who is not the founder once paid facilitators are engaged, plus a Deputy.
- Annual member-facing summary of where membership income went, complaints and incidents at aggregate level, and changes made as a result.
- Open complaints route that does not run through the person complained about.
- Guests, family, advisors and media may observe sessions on request where privacy and safeguarding allow.
---
## 11 · Strategic test for decisions
When making a product, staffing, marketing or commercial decision, ask:
1. Does this strengthen the weekly practice and real community?
1. Does it protect participant autonomy and safety?
1. Does it make follow-through more likely rather than simply adding more content?
1. Can we explain it transparently to members, parents, staff and partners?
1. Does it fit the actual scope of Mindcast?
1. Would we be comfortable if a member read the internal reasoning behind this decision?
---
## 12 · Founder notes
**What should never change as Mindcast scales?**
Participant autonomy, the anti-guru structure, and safeguarding. The curriculum, the format and the technology are all replaceable. These three are not.
**What may change as technology and delivery evolve?**
Delivery format, curation sources, pricing model, the software, and whether Mindcast operates in one town or twenty.
**Which value wins when commercial growth conflicts with participant safety or trust?**
Safety and trust, without exception. A single safeguarding or trust failure ends the organisation. Slower growth only delays it.
---
## 13 · How this charter is used
Every policy, contract, product decision and piece of marketing is tested against this document. If a proposal conflicts with Section 7, the proposal is dropped regardless of the revenue attached to it.
This charter is reviewed annually. Any amendment to Sections 6 or 7 is recorded in writing with the reason and notified to members.
> **Professional review.** The structure, employment, participant, privacy and safeguarding documents must receive appropriate New Zealand professional review before they are relied on in production.
---

title: Accessibility Statement
body:
## Accessibility Statement
Mindcast aims to make its website, app, printed material and live sessions usable by as many people as possible. Our working standard for digital experiences is **WCAG 2.2 AA**.
## What we commit to
- Body text and interactive controls meet appropriate contrast requirements.
- Every interactive element has a visible keyboard focus state.
- Core member flows can be completed by keyboard.
- Layouts remain usable at 320px width and 200% zoom without loss of content.
- Motion respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Forms use clear labels, fieldsets and legends where appropriate.
- Important information is not communicated by colour alone.
- Printed and live-session alternatives are available when the app is inaccessible or unavailable.
## Known gaps
Accessibility is an ongoing product requirement. Any known unresolved accessibility defects are tracked in the App QA Checklist and must be prioritised according to impact.
## Tell us when we have got it wrong
Members and guests may raise an accessibility issue through the published contact/complaints route. Raising an accessibility issue will not affect membership or participation.
## Review

title: Membership Access & Pricing Model
body:
> **Mindcast Limited · Taupō, Aotearoa New Zealand**  
MC-MEM-106 · Version 1.0-working · August 2026 · Member-facing · **Supplemental**
## Commercial principle
Mindcast is a transparent for-profit business. There is no collection plate, tithe, expected donation or hidden contribution. The price of paid access is stated clearly and is intended to cover operating costs, reinvestment and profit.
## Sunday access model
- **Live Sunday session:** free to attend, subject to capacity and registration.
- **First visit:** recommended full interactive trial access at no charge so a new person can experience the product.
- **Returning non-member:** may attend the live session but does not receive continuing app access, saved interactive answers, digital workbook history or member-only tools.
- **Daily physical worksheet:** **$5 NZD** for a non-member who wants a take-home reflection sheet.
- **Paid member:** full interactive participation, digital workbook, saved reflections/history, progress/check-ins, member tools, all weekly worksheets and priority/guaranteed booking when capacity is constrained.
## Working launch pricing
- Founding Adult: **$29/week**, first 100 memberships, locked for 12 months.
- Standard Adult: **$35/week**.
- Teen: working target **$22/week**.
- Child add-on: working target **$15/week**.
- Family bundle: working target **$79/week** for two adults plus up to three children/teens.
- Supported/community membership: working target **$19/week**, eligibility/process to be approved before launch.
All amounts are working commercial assumptions until the founder and accountant approve GST treatment and final pricing.
## What the member pays for
The paid relationship is deliberately clear: the member is paying for the product and infrastructure around the room — interactive software, persistent personal journey, worksheets, facilitators, venue, safeguards, administration and product improvement.
## Funnel to measure
**Free Sunday attendee → first interactive trial → $5 worksheet / return visit → paid membership → retained member → referral.**
Track separately:
- weekly attendees;
- unique free attendees;
- active paid memberships;
- active participants covered by family memberships;
- free-to-paid conversion within 4 and 8 weeks;
- worksheet conversion;
- membership retention;
- blended revenue per paid membership.
Do not report every participant in a family bundle as a separate paying membership.

title: Safeguarding & Child Protection Policy
body:
> 🛡️ **Mindcast Limited · Taupō, Aotearoa New Zealand**  
MC-SAF-001 · Version 1.0 · August 2026 · Safeguarding
## Safeguarding & Child Protection Policy
How Mindcast keeps children, young people and vulnerable adults safe. This is the policy that everything else depends on. Read it before your first session, not after.
**Document owner:** Safeguarding Lead  
**Applies to:** Everyone — staff, contractors, volunteers, board, members  
**Next review:** February 2027  
**Status:** Live — annual review mandatory
> **Immediate danger: call 111.**  
Child-safety concern: Oranga Tamariki **0508 326 459**.  
Person in distress: **1737** — call or text.  
You do not need permission from anyone at Mindcast to make an emergency or statutory-safety call.
## 1 · Scope and principles
This policy applies across every Mindcast session, Life Group, event and online interaction.
1. **A child's safety comes before everything** — reputation, relationships and organisational discomfort.
1. **Workers report concerns; they do not decide whether they are serious enough.**
1. **We report what we see or hear, not what we can prove.** Investigation belongs to statutory authorities.
1. Children and young people are told who they can talk to, that concerns will be taken seriously, and that raising one will not get them in trouble.
1. **Everyone is checked** where the role requires it — including friends, family and the founder.
1. Concerns about a worker or the founder go through an independent route and never through the person complained about.
The legal framework to be monitored includes the Children's Act 2014, Oranga Tamariki Act 1989, Crimes Act 1961, Privacy Act 2020, Health and Safety at Work Act 2015 and applicable safety-check regulations. The Professional & Legal Review Register is the source of truth for legal updates.
## 2 · Who is responsible
**Safeguarding Lead** — receives concerns, manages reporting, holds the restricted vetting register, oversees training and records. Once paid facilitators are engaged, this role must not be the founder.
**Deputy Safeguarding Lead** — acts when the Lead is unavailable or is the subject of the concern.
**Founder / Director** — resources the system and steps back entirely from any concern involving them.
**Independent Advisory Group** — at least three independent people; receives concerns about the founder or Safeguarding Lead and provides an external governance route.
**Every worker and volunteer** — reports every concern the same day. No exceptions.
Names/direct contacts are published on the website, session noticeboard and member/guardian induction material once appointments are complete.
## 3 · Safety checking
No one works or volunteers with children, young people or vulnerable adults until the required safety check is **complete and cleared**.
For a children's-worker role, complete the legally required components including identity, Police vetting where applicable, work history, relevant registration information, referee interviews/checks, interview and written risk assessment. Re-check at least every three years where required, or earlier under Mindcast policy/risk assessment.
A Police vet is an input, not the complete suitability decision. A person with a disqualifying/specified conviction must not be placed in a restricted role unless the applicable lawful exemption/process is satisfied.
Everyone must promptly disclose a charge, conviction, investigation or professional finding relevant to working with children or vulnerable people.
## 4 · Behaviour rules
### Never
- Be alone and out of sight with a child or young person who is not your own. If unavoidable for immediate safety, remain visible and report it afterwards.
- Privately message, text, call, video-call, email, follow or add a young member on personal social media.
- Transport a young person alone outside an approved arrangement.
- Give a young member money, gifts, food or a lift outside an agreed supervised arrangement.
- Photograph/video a child without the required written guardian consent.
- Use physical contact beyond what is appropriate, welcome and proportionate.
- Discuss your own romantic/sexual life with a young person.
- Promise secrecy to a child.
### Always
- Use **two safety-checked adults** for kids/teen sessions and any other role where the approved risk assessment requires it.
- Use shared/logged channels for young-member communications, with guardian visibility where required.
- Report any necessary boundary exception to the Safeguarding Lead the same day.
- Model the boundary consistently, including outside the room.
If a young person offers personal contact details, sends a social request or asks to talk privately, decline warmly, explain the boundary and notify the Safeguarding Lead where appropriate.
## 5 · Recognising concern
Workers are not diagnosing; they are noticing. Concerns may be physical, emotional/behavioural, neglect-related, direct/partial disclosures, or concerning adult behaviour such as secrecy, favouritism, gifts, attempts to isolate or repeated pressure for one-to-one contact.
**Grooming can look like kindness.** That is why the behaviour rules apply even to people we trust and like.
## 6 · If a child discloses to you
### Do
- Stay calm and listen at the child's pace.
- Believe and reassure them that telling was the right thing to do.
- Be honest that you need to tell the person responsible for keeping children safe.
- Use only open prompts such as “Can you tell me more about that?” where necessary.
- Record the child's own words as soon as possible, including date, time, place and who was present.
### Do not
- Promise secrecy.
- Ask leading questions or repeatedly question the child.
- Investigate or try to decide whether the allegation is true.
- show shock/anger in a way that burdens the child.
- Contact the alleged abuser or family before following the safeguarding escalation path where doing so could increase risk or compromise a response.
- Discuss the disclosure beyond the authorised safeguarding route.
## 7 · Escalation path
- **Immediate danger:** call 111, then notify the Safeguarding Lead.
- **Concern about a child's safety:** tell the Safeguarding Lead the same day and create the approved factual record within 24 hours.
- **Concern about a worker/volunteer/founder:** tell the Safeguarding Lead; if the concern is about the Lead, use the Deputy/Independent Advisory Group directly.
- **Mental distress/self-harm risk:** follow MC-SAF-002 Scope of Practice & Distress Escalation. Facilitators refer; they do not treat.
- A person may contact Police/Oranga Tamariki directly whenever they believe that is required; internal permission is not a prerequisite.
## 8 · Session and communication controls
- Two checked adults present for youth sessions.
- Young-member communications use approved logged channels.
- Guardian consent/permissions are recorded through the approved flow.
- Attendance/check-in does not expose a young person's private reflections.
- Kiosk/welcome-wall modes show only the minimum information required.
- Media use requires the specific consent appropriate to the person/guardian.
## 9 · Allegations involving staff
Protect the child/person first. Preserve evidence and records. Do not run an informal internal investigation that compromises a statutory investigation. Employment/process decisions are handled separately under MC-HR-008 with professional advice as needed.
No retaliation is permitted against a person who raises a safeguarding concern in good faith.
## 10 · Records and privacy
Safeguarding records contain the person's own words where relevant and clearly separate observed facts from opinion. Record what action was taken and who was notified.
Safeguarding records are stored **separately from ordinary member/personnel records**, encrypted and restricted to the Safeguarding Lead, Deputy and appropriately authorised governance/response people.
Working retention rule: **minimum seven years**, or longer where an authority/professional adviser directs. Privacy must never be used as a reason not to make a necessary child-safety report.
## 11 · Training
- **Everyone:** this policy, Code of Conduct and disclosure handling — before first session, then annually.
- **Kids/teen track workers:** full safeguarding module, scenarios and grooming recognition — before first session, then annually.
- **Facilitators:** above plus scope-of-practice/distress escalation; role-appropriate external first-aid/mental-health training where approved.
- **Safeguarding Lead:** external safeguarding training before/around appointment and refreshed on the approved cycle.
Training completion is recorded per person in MC-TRN-001 / the Staff Training portal and audited regularly. **Anyone overdue on a member-contact gate stands down from member-facing duties until it is current.**
## 12 · What members and whānau are told
At induction, on the website and at the venue, members/guardians are told:
- who the Safeguarding Lead/Deputy are and how to contact them;
- what safety-checking and adult-behaviour rules apply;
- how to raise a concern, including one about the founder;
- that raising a concern will never affect membership or participation.
## 13 · Review
Review annually and immediately after a serious safeguarding incident or material legal/operational change. The Safeguarding Lead signs off the review and the Independent Advisory Group notes it.
> **External review required:** MC-SAF-001 and MC-SAF-002 should be reviewed by an external safeguarding adviser before the first session with children/young people present. Any legal requirements should also be checked against current New Zealand guidance before launch.

title: Scope of Practice & Distress Escalation Protocol
body:
> **Mindcast facilitators refer. They do not diagnose, counsel or treat.**
## Purpose
This protocol defines the line between facilitated personal development and clinical care, and the escalation path when a member becomes distressed or discloses risk.
## Scope of practice
A Mindcast facilitator may:
- guide the published session structure;
- ask open reflective questions;
- normalise passing or taking a break;
- listen without diagnosing;
- help a person identify an appropriate support service;
- escalate safeguarding or immediate-safety concerns.
A facilitator must not:
- diagnose a mental-health condition;
- provide therapy, counselling or treatment;
- tell a member what trauma or symptom 'means';
- advise changing medication or medical treatment;
- promise confidentiality where safety is at risk;
- create a private dependency relationship;
- present themselves as a healer, clinician or authority.
## Distress during a session
1. Keep the room calm and preserve the person's dignity.
1. Offer the person the choice to pass, step outside or sit in the quiet space.
1. A second safety-checked worker checks on them where practicable; do not abandon the wider room.
1. Ask only what is necessary to understand immediate safety, not to investigate their history.
1. If there is immediate danger, call **111**.
1. If there is a child-protection concern, follow MC-SAF-001 immediately.
1. Where appropriate, provide referral information such as 1737 and relevant local services.
1. Record the incident/concern through the approved restricted process before the end of the required reporting window.
## Self-harm or suicide risk
If a person says they intend to harm themselves or someone else, has a plan or means, cannot stay safe, or presents an immediate serious risk, treat it as an urgent safety matter. Do not attempt to become their counsellor. Stay with the immediate safety need, involve emergency/clinical support, and escalate internally after the emergency response has begun.
## After the event
- Record facts separately from opinion.
- Notify the Safeguarding Lead where the concern is safeguarding-related.
- Debrief staff without disclosing unnecessary personal detail.
- Do not discuss the member's story outside the authorised response team.
- Review whether the session content, staffing or referral system needs to change.
## Training gate
Facilitators must pass the scope-of-practice and distress-escalation training module before member-facing duties and repeat it annually.

title: Information Security Policy
body:
## Information Security Policy
Mindcast protects member and staff information by limiting collection, access and exposure rather than relying on trust alone.
## Non-negotiable controls
- Row Level Security on every table containing personal data.
- Role checks use the existing server-controlled role system; users cannot self-escalate privilege.
- Service-role keys and other secrets never appear in client code, public repos, prompts, fixtures or screenshots.
- Production data is never copied into development/test; use synthetic data.
- MFA on privileged accounts.
- Preview/staging deployments are access-protected.
- Secrets are stored in the approved password manager and rotated after suspected exposure.
- Backups/PITR are configured and restoration is tested.
- Sentry/analytics are configured so member journal/reflection/safeguarding content is not transmitted.
## Sensitive content
Member reflections, child-safety records and personnel records receive the highest access restrictions. Safeguarding records are stored separately from ordinary operational records.
## AI
Follow MC-SEC-003. Real member/staff PII, journal content, safeguarding detail, credentials and environment files are prohibited in AI prompts unless an explicitly approved secure workflow says otherwise.
## Incident reporting
A suspected security/privacy incident is reported immediately through the approved incident route and handled under MC-SEC-002.

title: AI Use Policy
body:
## AI Use Policy
Mindcast uses AI tooling to build and improve systems, but member trust takes priority over convenience.
## Hard rules
- Never paste member journal/reflection text into a third-party model.
- Never paste safeguarding records, health information, staff personnel records or identifiable complaints into an AI tool.
- Never paste service-role keys, API secrets, `.env` files, credentials or private certificates into a prompt.
- Never use production personal data in AI-generated test fixtures or screenshots.
- Use synthetic data for development and training examples.
- Do not train third-party models on Mindcast member content.
- Obtain and record vendor settings/contractual position on model training and retention where an AI provider is used operationally.
## Approved uses
Generic coding questions, architecture discussion, copy editing without personal data, synthetic test generation, public-information research and curriculum drafting that does not expose member content.
## Product AI
Any member-facing AI insight feature must be opt-in, transparent about what data is processed, able to be disabled without losing the rest of the service, and covered by the privacy policy/data map.
## Review
New AI services require privacy/security review before real data is processed.

title: Staff Training Manual
body:
> 📘 **Mindcast Limited · Taupō, Aotearoa New Zealand**  
MC-TRN-001 · Version 1.0 · August 2026 · Training
## Staff Training Manual
Ten modules covering everything a person needs before they stand in a Mindcast room. This is the canonical source content for the interactive Staff Training portal: every checkpoint below becomes a recorded answer against the staff member's own profile.
**Document owner:** Safeguarding Lead  
**Applies to:** All employees, contractors and volunteers  
**Next review:** February 2027  
**Status:** Live — annual completion mandatory
## How this works
Ten modules. Work through them in order. Each has learning outcomes, training content and checkpoints.
**Modules 1, 3, 4, 5 and 6 must be complete and passed before member-facing work. Module 2 is required before the first session.** Modules 7 and 10 are due in Week 1; modules 8 and 9 are due within Month 1.
Everyone repeats the full manual **annually**. Anyone overdue on a member-contact gate **stands down from member-facing duties** until it is current.
### Module gates
1. **What Mindcast is** — before first session — acknowledgement.
1. **The room and the weekly ritual** — before first session — acknowledgement.
1. **Boundaries and the Code of Conduct** — before member contact — **100%**.
1. **Safeguarding children and young people** — before member contact — **100%**.
1. **Scope of practice and distress escalation** — before member contact — **100%**.
1. **Privacy and member confidentiality** — before member contact — **100%**.
1. **Security and the systems** — Week 1 — **80%**.
1. **Your employment** — Month 1 — acknowledgement.
1. **Money, expenses and conflicts** — Month 1 — **80%**.
1. **Speaking up and getting help** — Week 1 — acknowledgement.
## Module 1 · What Mindcast is
**Outcomes:** explain Mindcast to a stranger in 30 seconds · name the values · state the things we will never do.
### The problem
People consume enormous amounts of self-development and act on almost none of it. The gap is implementation. Mindcast supplies structure, rhythm, witness and a return date.
**Purpose:** Mindcast exists to close the gap between knowing and doing.  
**Mission:** To give every town a room where ordinary people become more themselves — together, every week, for as long as they want to keep coming.  
**Vision:** A world where every neighbourhood has a room you can walk into and become more yourself — together.
### How it works
A 52-week curriculum across adults, teens and children. Each week: live facilitated gathering, private reflection and a midweek Life Group. Members set an intention, return in seven days and are gently held to it.
### Values and hard limits
Community over content · draw out, do not preach · everyone can afford to belong · safe by design · honest about what we are · no pressure, ever.
We never position a guru; provide therapy/clinical care; make leaving costly; pressure attendance/payment; repurpose member words without specific consent; sell member data/use reflections to train third-party AI; or isolate people from family/friends/other communities.
### Checkpoints
- **1.1 · Free text:** In your own words, how would you explain Mindcast to someone who asked about it in a café?
- **1.2 · Multi-select:** Which of these is Mindcast? Therapy · a facilitated personal development community · a church · a weekly in-person gathering · a coaching business · a 52-week programme for adults, teens and kids.
- **1.3 · Free text:** A member says “you've changed my life, you're basically my therapist.” What is wrong with accepting that, and what would you say?
- **1.4 · Acknowledgement:** I have read MC-GOV-001 Company Charter and understand its hard limits.
## Module 2 · The room and the weekly ritual
**Outcomes:** run the session flow · know the role/handover points · set the room up safely.
### Ritual
Arrive → NFC check-in → welcome wall → facilitated session → private reflection → Life Group invitation.
**The ritual is the product.** Members are not coming for novelty; they are coming for the reliability of the same healthy practice happening at the same time with people who know them.
### Before doors open
- Venue walk-through; hazards/cables/exits/lighting checked.
- First-aid kit present; AED location known.
- Two required safety-checked adults on site before youth/member activity begins.
- AV tested and Facilitator View on the correct week.
- Referral cards available.
- Quiet space available/signposted.
- Kids/teen spaces appropriately staffed.
- First aider and safeguarding contact identified.
- Content warning prepared where relevant.
### During and after
Welcome people by name · watch the room rather than the screen · pass means pass · leaving mid-session is allowed · sharing is opt-in/moderated · debrief after every session · escalate worries same night · record attendance/incidents · pack down safely.
### Checkpoints
- **2.1 · Ordering:** Put the ritual in order: private reflection · NFC check-in · facilitated session · arrival and welcome · Life Group invitation · welcome wall.
- **2.2 · Scenario/free text:** Your co-worker cannot attend. You are the only safety-checked adult available and the kids track has eight children booked. What do you do?
- **2.3 · Single select:** A member walks out mid-session. Choose the safe response: signal a co-worker to check quietly while the facilitator holds the room.
- **2.4 · Checklist:** Complete the pre-session checklist from memory, then compare.
## Module 3 · Boundaries and the Code of Conduct
**Outcomes:** state boundaries without looking them up · recognise dual relationships · know serious misconduct. **Pass mark: 100%.**
### Boundaries
- Confidentiality: only safety/legal exceptions.
- Stay in your lane: facilitate; do not counsel, diagnose, treat or advise.
- No romantic/sexual relationship with a member you facilitate; declare existing overlaps.
- No money/borrowing/lending/selling between workers and members; gifts/conflicts declared under policy.
- No one-to-one or private-channel relationships with young people.
- No guru behaviour or private following-building.
- No recruiting members into another business, cause, church, MLM, political campaign or personal practice.
- No guilt, shame, urgency or social cost to make someone attend, stay, pay, share or believe.
- Every safeguarding concern is reported the same day.
Serious misconduct may include confidentiality/safeguarding breaches, prohibited relationships, violence/threats, harassment, theft/fraud/falsification, impairment at work, deliberate unauthorised data access and retaliation against someone who raises a concern, subject to a fair process.
### Checkpoints
- **3.1 · Scenario/free text:** A member you facilitate asks you out for coffee clearly as a date. What do you do and who do you tell?
- **3.2 · Scenario/free text:** Your sister is a member of the Life Group you lead. Is this a problem? What do you do?
- **3.3 · Multi-select:** Identify serious misconduct among confidentiality disclosure, private commercial selling, prohibited one-to-one youth contact and other scenarios.
- **3.4 · Single select:** A 16-year-old sends you a friend request. Correct response: decline, explain the boundary warmly and tell the Safeguarding Lead where appropriate.
- **3.5 · Acknowledgement:** I have read and signed MC-HR-004 Staff Code of Conduct and understand boundary breaches may be serious misconduct.
## Module 4 · Safeguarding children and young people
**Outcomes:** recognise concern · handle a disclosure correctly · escalate immediately. **Pass mark: 100%; repeat annually.**
### Three rules
1. A child's safety comes before everything.
1. You do not decide whether a concern is serious enough — report it.
1. Report what you see/hear; investigation belongs to statutory authorities.
Never isolate a child/young person; privately message/follow/call them; transport alone outside an approved arrangement; give gifts outside policy; photograph without consent; or promise confidentiality. Work to the approved two-adult/supervision model and use logged guardian-visible channels where required.
Grooming can look like kindness. Rules apply equally to long-standing and well-liked people.
### Disclosure handling
Stay calm · listen · believe · reassure · explain that you must tell the safeguarding person · record the child's own words. Do not promise secrecy, ask leading questions, investigate, repeatedly question, contact an alleged abuser prematurely or discuss the matter outside the safeguarding response.
### Escalation
Immediate danger → 111 then Safeguarding Lead.  
Child-safety concern → Safeguarding Lead same day.  
Concern about worker/founder → Safeguarding Lead or independent route if the Lead is involved.  
Unsure → report anyway.
### Checkpoints
- **4.1 · Scenario/free text:** A 9-year-old says “I don't want to go home tonight.” What do you say, what do you not say, and what happens next?
- **4.2 · Multi-select:** Identify correct disclosure responses: thank/believe, open question, factual record; reject secrecy/leading questions/premature parent contact.
- **4.3 · Single select:** You are unsure whether a concern is serious enough. Correct response: tell the Safeguarding Lead today.
- **4.4 · Scenario/free text:** A long-standing volunteer gives a teen lifts and messages privately, saying they are only helping. What is your obligation and to whom?
- **4.5 · Recall/free text:** Name the Safeguarding Lead and Deputy and how to contact them, without looking it up.
- **4.6 · Acknowledgement:** I have read MC-SAF-001 and understand I must report every concern the same day.
## Module 5 · Scope of practice and distress escalation
**Outcomes:** know the facilitator/clinician boundary · respond to distress without rescuing · handle suicide-risk disclosures safely. **Pass mark: 100%.**
### Your role
You are a facilitator: hold the room, ask questions, keep time and make it safe to think out loud. In a Mindcast role you are not acting as a therapist, counsellor, psychologist, social worker, coach, doctor or crisis worker — even if qualified elsewhere.
In scope: open questions, reflecting back, recognising struggle, silence, empathy and referral.  
Out of scope: interpretation, diagnosis, relationship/health/legal/financial advice, ongoing private support, trauma processing, medication advice or “what you need to do is…”
### Distress
Stay calm · do not treat tears as an emergency · offer choice · signal a co-worker · use quiet space · avoid debriefing/processing · offer referral information · escalate/record appropriately · use one proportionate follow-up only if policy requires.
### Suicide/self-harm risk
Take it seriously. Ask directly about immediate safety/suicide risk, stay with the person, involve the Safeguarding Lead/emergency/clinical support, do not promise secrecy or attempt therapy, and call 111 for immediate danger. Follow MC-SAF-002.
### Checkpoints
- **5.1 · Free text:** Write what you would say to a member who starts crying in a session.
- **5.2 · Single select:** A member discloses suicidal thoughts. Correct response: ask directly about safety/suicide risk, stay with them and get the Safeguarding Lead/emergency support as needed.
- **5.3 · Multi-select:** Identify out-of-scope actions including medication advice and interpretive/diagnostic statements.
- **5.4 · Free text:** A member privately messages you three times asking to talk. What do you do?
- **5.5 · Recall:** Write down 1737 and two other approved referral/emergency contacts without looking.
## Module 6 · Privacy and member confidentiality
**Outcomes:** know what you may access · recognise a privacy breach · report quickly. **Pass mark: 100%.**
The most sensitive information we hold is what people wrote about their own lives believing it was private. **Facilitators cannot see private journals.** If role permissions reveal content they should not, treat that as a security/privacy incident.
### Three promises
1. We do not sell/rent/trade personal information.
1. Private reflections stay private unless the member intentionally shares a specific item.
1. We do not use member reflections to train third-party AI models.
### Worker rules
Access only what your role requires · no screenshots/exports/personal cloud · no member content in AI tools · Bcc or approved mailing tool for bulk mail · verify recipients · lock screens · confidentiality continues after leaving.
### Checkpoints
- **6.1 · Multi-select:** Identify privacy breaches among visible-recipient bulk email, unauthorised journal access, AI-pasting and exposed attendance records; distinguish lawful safeguarding reporting.
- **6.2 · Free text:** You emailed a newsletter with all recipients visible. What do you do and by when?
- **6.3 · Single select:** A member you know socially stopped attending. Do not access their journal; use an ordinary respectful contact route if appropriate.
- **6.4 · Acknowledgement:** I have read MC-MEM-002 Privacy Policy and signed the confidentiality obligations; I understand they continue after I leave.
## Module 7 · Security and the systems
**Outcomes:** use systems safely · apply least privilege · report an incident fast. **Pass mark: 80%.**
MFA on privileged accounts · individual logins · least privilege · password manager · secure/updated devices · no member data on personal devices · report lost devices/suspicious logins immediately.
### If you build or prompt
- RLS on every personal-data table.
- Role checks use the existing `has_role()` / `user_roles` model; never a user-editable profile role.
- Service-role keys never appear in client code, repo or AI prompts.
- Separate test/live Stripe keys.
- Synthetic data only in dev/test.
- AI-generated migrations get an explicit RLS review every time.
### Checkpoints
- **7.1 · Single select:** You want to export a member table to a laptop for convenience. Correct response: ask the Technical Lead/use the approved safer workflow; do not export casually.
- **7.2 · Multi-select:** Identify what must never enter an AI prompt: member journal/email/PII, service-role keys, `.env` files and other secrets.
- **7.3 · Free text:** You notice you can see another person's reflection. What is it and what do you do?
- **7.4 · Acknowledgement:** I have read MC-SEC-001 Information Security Policy and MC-SEC-003 AI Use Policy.

## Module 9 · Money, expenses and conflicts
**Outcomes:** claim expenses correctly · recognise/declare conflicts. **Pass mark: 80%.**
Use documented spending/approval limits. Nobody approves their own claim. Keep receipts and business purpose. Member income flows through company systems, never personal accounts. Do not borrow/lend or sell private services to members. Declare outside work, family/romantic/financial interests and material gifts/conflicts; step out of affected decisions.

- **9.2 · Multi-select:** Identify reportable conflicts including close relationships with members/suppliers, outside coaching/wellness work, related suppliers and material gifts.

## Module 10 · Speaking up and getting help
**Outcomes:** know multiple routes to raise concerns · know they apply to the founder · know where to get support.
### Routes
1. A facilitator/manager for an ordinary room/work issue.
1. `concerns@mindcast.co.nz` for concerns/complaints.
1. Safeguarding Lead for child/young-person/safety matters.
1. Independent Advisory Group for concerns about the founder/Safeguarding Lead or where the internal route is not trusted.
The person complained about never handles the complaint. Good-faith reporting must not cause retaliation. People may also use external statutory/professional routes without exhausting Mindcast's process first.
Worker wellbeing is part of safety: post-session debrief, supervision/support appropriate to role and permission to say when you are not fit to hold the room.
### Checkpoints
